label: Canakinumab (Ilaris) — SJIA · Sun 2016 / EMA II/0026 · 2-compartment SC
_note: The pooled canakinumab PK-binding model re-estimated for the SJIA indication (28 studies; 201 SJIA patients). The drug PK part is used; the IL-1beta binding part is not simulated. Headline values match the Sun 2016 abstract exactly, so the EMA table is taken as the same model (inference).

_source.document: EMA assessment report EMEA/H/C/001109/II/0026 (Ilaris SJIA variation, 2013)
_source.table: Table 9 (parameters), Table 7 (population), Table 2 and p.23 (exposures); cross-checked with Sun et al. 2016, J Clin Pharmacol (doi:10.1002/jcph.754), abstract
_source.subjects: Pooled 28 studies (CAPS, gout, RA, healthy volunteers, psoriasis, SJIA); SJIA subset N=201, age 1-19 y

limitations: The age effect on the absorption rate (exponent −0.292) is disabled because the report gives no reference age, and the tabulated absorption rate (0.295/day) is used at all ages. The younger the patient, the more absorption may be computed as slower than it really is.
The form of the residual error (25.7%) is not specified, so it is assumed proportional. Between-subject variability in bioavailability was not reported.
IL-1β binding (Kd 1.5 nM) is not simulated; only the drug part is used.
Only the mean weight of 32.8 (SD 21.0) is available, so the distribution is approximated as log-normal with median 33 kg and CV 64% (the resulting mean is higher than the actual one).
This source is not the paper (Sun 2016) itself but the EMA assessment report presenting the same analysis. The paper is paywalled, so only its abstract was checked.
